records.issue_text: Making .small-action a flex container lays children (button, .small-action-desc) side-by-side in a row instead of stacked, breaking multi-line descriptions and multi-child small-action variants on narrow widths
records.rationale: The diff changes `.small-action` to `@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);` without setting `flex-direction: column;` or allowing wrapping. By default, flex containers lay direct children out in a single row, so if `.small-action` previously relied on normal block flow to stack multiple children (e.g., a button and `.small-action-desc`, or multi-child variants), this change can force side-by-side layout and cause narrow-width/multi-line layout breakage. The diff does not contradict this mechanism.

records.issue_text: -moz-inline-box and -ms-align-items are invalid property names that Sass will emit verbatim as dead declarations, potentially causing misaligned category bullets on browsers honoring only unprefixed flex
records.rationale: The diff’s `@mixin align-items($alignment)` already includes the correct properties (`-ms-flex-align: $alignment;` and `align-items:$alignment;`), so the extra `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` being ignored would not “potentially caus[e] misaligned category bullets on browsers honoring only unprefixed flex.” The same mixin sets unprefixed `align-items`, and `@mixin inline-flex()` sets `display: inline-flex;`, so modern browsers honoring only unprefixed flex will use those rather than be affected by any dead prefixed declarations.
